note_text: Situation: 68-year-old female post-emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis, currently stable but with mild tachycardia and low-grade fever. Background: History of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity; no prior abdominal surgeries. On enoxaparin started 24 hours ago for DVT prophylaxis. Foley catheter removed 12 hours ago. Assessment: Vitals show temperature 37.8 degrees C, HR 102 bpm, BP 130/78 mmHg, RR 20, O2 sat 94% on nasal cannula 2 L/min. Wound clean with mild erythema. No bleeding concerns. Moderate fall risk, low delirium risk. Pending labs: CBC, blood cultures, BMP; pending abdominal ultrasound for fluid collection. Recommendation: Continue monitoring vitals and oxygen support. Monitor platelet counts and bleeding signs daily due to enoxaparin. Surgical team to reassess in 6 hours. Family updated today and available for contact if condition changes.

note_text: Situation: 78-year-old female admitted with acute decompensated heart failure and volume overload. Background: History includes chronic heart failure with reduced EF, hypertension, CKD stage 3, and atrial fibrillation. Currently on furosemide 40 mg daily (recently increased), lisinopril, apixaban, and metoprolol. Allergic to penicillin (rash). Assessment: Vitals show mild hypoxia on 2L nasal cannula, tachypnea, and stable hemodynamics. Bilateral lower extremity edema and mild JVD noted. Labs pending: daily BMP, INR, NT-proBNP; chest X-ray pending. No infection or bleeding concerns currently. Moderate fall risk and low delirium risk. Code status full. Recommendation: Continue current diuretics and anticoagulation with INR and renal monitoring. Monitor oxygen requirements and escalate to ICU if respiratory or hemodynamic status worsens. Daily clinical assessments and labs required. Family updated; daughter is primary contact.

note_text: Situation: 72F postop emergency laparotomy for perforated diverticulitis, currently unstable with borderline sepsis signs. Background: History of HTN, T2DM, CKD stage 3, prior cholecystectomy. Allergic to penicillin (rash). On IV piperacillin-tazobactam, insulin sliding scale, acetaminophen, low-dose aspirin. Assessment: Vitals abnormal (T 37.8 degrees C, HR 105, BP 110/65, RR 22, O2 sat 94% on 2L NC). Alert but mildly confused. Wound clean with moderate serous drainage, minimal bleeding. Foley catheter in place, urine output adequate. Infection concern for possible intra-abdominal abscess. Recommendation: Monitor vitals closely, continue antibiotics, maintain oxygen support, pending blood cultures, daily labs, and abdominal CT within 24 hours. Watch for worsening infection or bleeding. Family updated; full code status maintained.

note_text: Situation: Elderly female, 72 years old, post emergency laparotomy for perforated diverticulitis, currently showing signs of borderline sepsis and unstable vitals. Background: Past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease stage 3, and previous cholecystectomy. She is allergic to penicillin which causes rash. She is currently receiving IV piperacillin-tazobactam and insulin sliding scale with acetaminophen for pain and low dose aspirin daily. Assessment: Vital signs are abnormal with temperature 37.8 degrees C, heart rate 105 bpm, blood pressure 110/65 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 94% on 2L nasal cannula. The patient is alert but mildly confused. Wound is clean with moderate serous drainage and minimal bleeding. Foley catheter is in place with adequate urine output. Infection concern remains for possible intra-abdominal abscess. Fall and delirium risks are present. note_text: Situation: Elderly female admitted for acute exacerbation of chronic heart failure with volume overload. Background: She has a history of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation on apixaban, hypertension, chronic kidney disease stage 3, and osteoarthritis. Recent medication changes include an increase in furosemide dose from 20 mg to 40 mg daily three days ago due to worsening edema. Assessment: Currently, she is alert but mildly confused, with bilateral lower extremity edema and jugular venous distension. Vitals show tachycardia, mild hypoxia requiring 2L oxygen via nasal cannula, and blood pressure elevated at 145/90. Foley catheter inserted two days ago for urine output monitoring. There is a moderate fall risk and delirium risk present. Bleeding risk is low but monitored due to anticoagulation. Infection risk is low. Recommendation: Continue current medications with careful titration of diuretics to avoid electrolyte imbalance. Monitor renal function and signs of bleeding daily. Pending labs include daily electrolytes, renal function panel, BNP, and INR. Chest X-ray is pending to assess pulmonary congestion. Daily clinical and lab reassessment is required. Family has been updated and is involved in care planning. Code status is full. Close monitoring is essential to detect any deterioration.

note_text: Situation: 78F admitted with acute exacerbation of chronic heart failure presenting with volume overload. Background: History includes CHF with reduced EF, HTN, T2DM, CKD stage 3, prior ischemic stroke without deficits. Currently on furosemide 40 mg daily (increased 2 days ago), lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, and apixaban. Allergic to penicillin (rash). Assessment: Vitals show mild tachypnea and borderline hypoxia on 2 L nasal cannula. Physical exam reveals bilateral lower extremity edema and bibasilar crackles. Urine output adequate via indwelling catheter placed yesterday. Labs pending: daily BMP, NT-proBNP, INR. Imaging pending: chest X-ray. Risks include bleeding due to anticoagulation with renal impairment, fall risk, and infection risk from catheter. Code status is full code. Recommendation: Continue current meds and oxygen support. Monitor labs and imaging results daily. Escalate to ICU if respiratory status worsens or bleeding occurs. Family updated yesterday.
